newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call money inches up on increased demand.
newsitem.headline: Manila call money inches up on increased demand.

text.p: * Average interbank call rate up at 11.625 pct
The Philippine interbank call loan rate inched up to 11.625 percent from Tuesday's 11.21875 percent due to higher demand for pesos, traders said.
Borrowers were led by big banks which have to cover their two-day reserve deficiencies. The interbank market was closed on Wednesday for Christmas.
The improving health of President Fidel Ramos has already been discounted by the market, the added.
One trader added that a possibility of a long New Year weekend also prompted banks to beef up their liquidity position.
"Some banks were still trying to prop up their year-end financial positions," one trader said.

The Central Bank has yet to announce a holiday on December 31, but bankers said it has always been a banking holiday. The market will be closed on December 30 and January 1 for national public holidays.
Turnover was heavy with 30.333 billion pesos changing hands among 36 lenders and 24 borrowers. Done rates ranged from 10.8125 percent to 12.25 percent.
The secondary market for government securities was quiet, since many of the traders were on vacation.
One bank did not give its two-way quotes, saying that its traders were taking the next two days off.
"Many of the traders have already closed their books for the year," one trader said. Three-month bills were being bid at 11.525 to 11.85 percent, and offered at 11.425 to 11.725 percent.
Six-month bills were being bought at 11.8 to 12.10 percent and sold at 11.70 to 11.90 percent. One-year bills were being bid at 12.5 to 13.0 percent and sold at 12.30 to 12.50 percent.
